title: Neural evidence that dogs segment the speech they hear with a humanlike consonant bias
title_zh: 犬类在听到人类语音时表现出类似人类的辅音偏好，神经证据表明其能进行语音分割
abstract: Across many human languages, consonants carry more lexical information than vowels. During speech segmentation, humans, unlike nonhuman primates, rely more on consonant than vowel patterns, despite vowels’ greater acoustic saliency. To investigate whether this consonant bias is specific to humans or could also emerge in other species exposed to human speech, we performed noninvasive electroencephalography in humans and dogs. Intertrial coherence measures of neural entrainment and event-related potentials revealed enhanced word-level tracking for consonant- compared with vowel-structured streams in both species. This suggests that dogs, similar to humans, exhibit consonant bias when segmenting the speech they hear. Linguistic regularity–based processing biases can thus also emerge in a nonspeaking species exposed to speech.
abstract_zh: 在许多人类语言中，辅音携带的词汇信息多于元音。在语音分割过程中，人类（与非人类灵长类动物不同）更依赖辅音而非元音模式，尽管元音的声学显著性更高。为探究这种辅音偏好是否仅限于人类，或在接触人类语音的其他物种中也会出现，我们对人类和犬类进行了无创脑电图（EEG）记录。神经同步性（intertrial coherence）和事件相关电位（ERP）测量显示，两种物种在辅音结构流中对词级跟踪的增强明显高于元音结构流。这表明犬类与人类类似，在分割所听语音时也表现出辅音偏好。基于语言规律的处理偏好因此也可在接触语音的非说话物种中出现。
